arguments.prompt:
Create a professional native pixel-art combat animation source atlas of Meryl Silverburgh, exactly her adult Metal Gear Solid (1998) original PlayStation incarnation. Appearance: athletic adult woman with short red/orange hair and a dark burgundy bandana, olive-green sleeveless tank top, grey combat cargo trousers, black tactical belt, black combat boots, fingerless gloves, and her physical large silver Desert Eagle pistol. Do not use her later MGS4 uniform or a cap, camouflage coat, long hair or a different gun. Recognizable clean detailed 16-bit game sprites. Every figure is complete head to boots with the entire pistol inside its own cell, all facing screen-right in the same three-quarter side view. Same anatomical body scale and costume in all poses; crouched poses remain naturally shorter.

STRICT LAYOUT: exactly FORTY-EIGHT separate figures in EIGHT COLUMNS and SIX ROWS, a regular 8 by 6 grid. Transparent background. No text, labels, numbers, drawn grid, panels, floor, cast shadow, scenery or other people. Generous transparent gaps between figures and generous outer margins, absolutely no cropped body or weapon. Every successive group of four images is a genuine FOUR-FRAME animation with four different drawn poses; never duplicate complete figures.

ROW 1 columns 1–4 INTRO: calmly check the pistol held low, raise to readiness, settle; columns 5–8 OUTRO: lower the pistol, turn slightly, step to leave, settle.
ROW 2 columns 1–4 ROUND VICTORY: relaxed alert stance, small confident head nod, lower shoulders, settle; columns 5–8 ROUND DEFEAT: catch breath, stoop slightly, steady herself, recover.
ROW 3 columns 1–4 FINISHING PRESENTATION: disciplined two-handed pistol aim, sight alignment, brief ordinary pistol recoil, lower barrel. No victim or injury; columns 5–8 MATCH VICTORY: restrained salute with free hand, lower hand, relieved posture, settle, visibly distinct from round victory.
ROW 4 columns 1–4 MATCH DEFEAT: slowly crouch onto one knee, bow head, recover balance, settle, no injury; columns 5–8 SUPER: separate new four-frame two-handed precision Desert Eagle shot, brace, aim, recoil and return to ready, different drawings from the finishing sequence.
ROW 5 columns 1–4 IDLE: subtle breathing and weight transfer with pistol held low; columns 5–8 RUN: natural four-frame locomotion with pistol retained safely close to torso.
ROW 6 columns 1–4 ORDINARY ATTACK: one clean aimed pistol shot, distinct four poses from super; columns 5–8 HIT REACTION: non-graphic recoil, guard, regain posture, settle.

Each firing sequence has only a TINY conventional muzzle flash attached to the pistol barrel in its third frame. No flash or shot in intros, outros, victory, defeat, idle, run or hit reaction. No beam, magic, aura, floating bullet, projectile trail or invented power. Solo non-graphic acting only: no blood, wounds, severing, corpse or death spectacle. The forty-eight drawings must be genuinely distinct and preserve the selected 1998 character and equipment.
